title: Continuing Harness: Project Setup and the Epoch–Sync Loop

text.insert: This review spec defines project setup and a continuing per-game harness: initial Sync, Run epochs, automatic Sync between epochs, and durable timeline evidence. It combines the agreed lifecycle direction with proposed configuration and recovery contracts. The runtime still uses cycles; implementation and cycle removal follow review of this spec.

text.insert: The host runs orchestration, model sessions, integration, and game-owned knowledge. Daytona supplies isolated claim workspaces for source edits, compilation, and scoring. Each claim starts from the accepted harness head. Its patch returns to the host for validation and serialized integration.

Shared GameCube tools declare compiler and build-layout requirements. Each game supplies bindings, target region, original input identities, compiler pins, and an accepted sandbox profile. A different checkout alone is insufficient while tools still assume Melee paths.

The reviewed target separates shared application code, configuration, and service runtime data from each game's config, workspace, knowledge, and runtime groups. Keep .pi-sessions in its current location. Keep ref, ai_docs, and other extra folders for now. This tree describes a later migration; existing environment loaders and persisted path references must be updated before moving their files.

entries.note: Compiler, target, commands, and report paths
Keep transcripts here for this cleanup; do not redistribute
Game build output; equivalent claim-local output stays in Daytona

text.insert: The only existing top-level folder selected for retirement in this cleanup is projects. Reconcile its remaining PR-library files and update old path references before removal. Do not infer that it is unused from its name or the stale symlink comment. Backups and checkout-local state require separate review; they are not selected for deletion.

Do not introduce a separate general-purpose logs directory. Agent Kernel owns structured traces; required stdout/stderr files remain operation evidence or process diagnostics referenced by their owning records. Existing file consumers must be migrated before those files can be removed. Game build output belongs inside the game checkout or Daytona claim workspace; frontend build output belongs under apps/frontend/dist. A root build directory is not part of the target layout.

These shapes describe resolved logical configuration, not existing API schemas. The small game.json entry point references files under config. Resolve relative paths from the game root consistently, including config/local.json overrides. Credentials remain references.

text.insert: Acquisition captures raw inputs. Import normalizes archival records. Search indexing makes records retrievable. Librarian backfill curates facts and relationships with citations. Backfill is not a synonym for download or import; each stage records completion independently.

Rerunning the same capture must not duplicate records or work. Partial fetches retain resumable cursors without advancing past gaps. Changed upstream text creates a new capture while existing citations remain resolvable. Keep source data game-scoped; reusable cross-game facts require explicit applicability.

steps.text: Resolve Project Configuration
Validate identity, repository, target/build profile, tools, and declared external sources.
Report missing required credentials or capabilities without treating missing data as an empty source.
Establish the Harness Worktree
Clone or adopt the configured checkout and record its source identity.
Build and validate the selected target; derive report targets and source entities before curation.
Seed Configured Knowledge
Capture initial PR, Discord, and wiki material according to declared scope.
Import immutable records and build search indexes.
Queue or run librarian backfill; record which subjects and source captures were covered.
Verify Execution and Readiness
Verify the accepted game image and seed one representative claim workspace.
Compile and score against the host baseline; verify source citations resolve.
Require the configured bootstrap gates, with optional unfinished curation visibly pending.
Record Initial Boundary
Persist accepted head, upstream baseline, configuration provenance, and initial save point.
Enable Run admission only after readiness succeeds. Resume interrupted setup from durable stage results.

text.insert: Proposed bootstrap default: required source acquisition, import, and search indexes must complete; mechanical target/entity extraction and build evidence must be valid. Full semantic curation can continue in the background with visible coverage. Whether a first curated pass must also gate Run is an open review decision.

text.insert: These operation names express the proposed interface. Every mutation carries the selected game, a command identity, and expected state revision. Retries reconcile existing work instead of starting duplicate workflows.

operations.name: initializeProject
operations.description: Resolve the project and start resumable bootstrap Sync. Refuse identity mismatch or incomplete required configuration.

operations.name: requestRun
operations.description: Record desired Run state. Admit an epoch only after readiness and required Sync succeed.

operations.name: requestPause
operations.description: Stop new admission and settle active work. Preserve desired pause through subsequent Sync.
operations.returns: Pause request and eventual settled boundary

operations.name: requestSync
operations.description: Bootstrap, epoch-triggered, or manual entry to the same staged workflow. Queue behind active claims and integration.
operations.returns: Sync identity and completion or recovery state

operations.name: getTimeline
operations.description: Read ordered evidence without rebuilding or changing the worktree.
operations.returns: Boundary events, evidence links, and freshness

steps.text: Admit an Epoch
Use accepted head, valid report, and current target eligibility.
Pin claim bases and record the knowledge provenance used.
Run Workers
Edit and score isolated Daytona workspaces.
Integrate validated results serially and queue outcome knowledge processing.
Settle the Epoch Boundary
Finish claims and integration; measure the accepted epoch result.
Record epoch evidence and its save point before upstream reconciliation.
Run Sync
Refresh upstream and due source inputs; stage and validate reconciliation.
Apply accepted source changes; record Sync completion even when head is unchanged.
Capture required post-sync evidence and preserve unresolved failures.
Refresh and Continue
Recompute or validate report/board data for the accepted post-sync head.
Start the next epoch only when gates pass and desired state remains Run.
Otherwise remain paused, blocked, or idle without closing the harness.

text.insert: The sequence shows intended behavior. If epoch settlement or its required evidence fails, block before handing off to Sync. If source application succeeds but evidence capture fails, retain the accepted source head and retry capture; do not replay or undo publication merely because evidence is missing.

Automatic Sync runs after every settled epoch. Wiki refresh can remain explicit or scheduled; each Sync checks source policy rather than remirroring everything. Background fetching may overlap Run, but source publication cannot race claims or integration.

text.insert: Save points pin measurements and artifacts to an existing commit. They do not create commits or guarantee a complete restore of knowledge and runtime state. A no-source-change Sync may reuse verified build evidence if build inputs remain identical. Knowledge revision and source refresh outcomes remain independently visible.

Compare scores only for the same target scope, build configuration, and metric definition. Missing or stale evidence is not zero progress. Head changes, dirty worktrees, failed capture, or changed build inputs invalidate current-score claims. Dashboard reads never trigger a build.

rows: Fetch/import/index failure
Keep successful stage results and cursors; required stages block admission, optional gaps remain visible.
Source conflict or validation failure
Retain staging and diagnostic evidence; keep accepted head unchanged until reconciliation succeeds.
Crash during source application
Recover Git position and state publication as one coordinated operation; never assume Git and SQL share a transaction.
Repeated command or boundary retry
Use stable operation IDs; do not duplicate integration, timeline entries, imports, or counted gains.
Pause or restart
Reconcile leases, claims, accepted worktree, and pending publication; keep desired pause and history.

text.insert: This document does not authorize deleting historical evidence or changing the running system. The later migration removes cycles from runtime ownership, APIs, UI, and active documentation after their responsibilities and references have moved.

steps.text: Freeze the Reviewed Contract
Resolve the open decisions below and finalize state, source, and event schemas.
Migrate Durable Ownership
Back up state and inventory cycle references, source lineage, worktree identities, leases, and evidence links.
Move ownership and paths into the reviewed folder layout, updating stored references while preserving canonical worktree identity.
Preserve historical evidence and causal IDs in migrated records or a historical archive.
Switch Runtime Consumers
Update worktree resolution, Sync, Run, recovery, process identity, tracing, and dashboard projections.
Remove cycle open/close commands and all runtime dependencies on cycle IDs.
Prove the Replacement
Verify bootstrap, multi-epoch Sync, pause/resume, and injected failure recovery.
Check pre/post migration head, evidence counts, identities, metrics, and citation resolution.
Remove Superseded Documentation and Storage
Rewrite owning contracts and custom diagrams around the reviewed flow; repair references and examples.
Retire old schema/code only after compatibility and recovery checks pass. Preserve a recoverable migration checkpoint.

rows: New game bootstrap
Explicit game configuration produces valid build, sandbox, required source stages, citations, and an initial boundary without creating a cycle.
Two successive epochs
Each epoch has distinct evidence, a following Sync result, and admission pinned to the accepted post-sync head.
No-change and source-changing Sync
Both appear in history; only accepted source changes move head; worker and upstream deltas stay separate.
Pause, crash, or partial failure
Recovery preserves desired state, resumes durable stages, and does not duplicate integration or counted evidence.
Migration and game isolation
Old evidence remains resolvable, active consumers require no cycle ID, and a second game cannot read or write Melee-owned state by default.
Initial curation gate
Require imported/searchable sources and mechanical entities; show full semantic backfill as pending until complete. Decide whether a first curated pass also gates Run.
Long-lived run identity
Keep one run across automatic Sync handoffs; record process sessions separately. Epoch and Sync IDs remain distinct.
Missing external source
Require an explicit disabled/unavailable reason. Fail only declared required readiness gates.
Resource and publication policy
Keep source-specific refresh cadence and existing validation gates. Define credentials and external PR publication separately.
Second portability target
Choose a second GameCube decomp repository before claiming the contract supports multiple games.
